name: html-body-overflow-x-hidden-prevents-document-level-scroll
hook: Global overflow-x:hidden on html+body prevents horizontal scroll at document root
body:
Always set `overflow-x: hidden` on both html and body elements in globals.css. Without this, any overflowing child element (KaTeX, wide tables, fixed-width cards, padded LaTeX viewers) creates page-level horizontal scroll. Inner containers that legitimately need horizontal scroll (tables, code blocks, math overflow) keep their own overflow-x:auto. 

**Why:** KaTeX-display has overflow-x:auto internally, but if the document root allows horizontal scroll, the browser shows scrollbars at the page level even though inner content could scroll on its own. The global overflow-x:hidden on html/body prevents document-level scroll while inner containers with overflow-x:auto handle their own horizontal scroll correctly.

**How to apply:** Add `overflow-x: hidden` to html and body in globals.css @layer base. This is a foundational CSS fix that should be in every project.

name: mobile-padding-must-be-responsive
hook: Fixed large padding (px-12) on mobile causes overflow with max-w containers
body:
Fixed pixel padding like px-12 (48px per side) combined with max-w-[794px] creates 890px total width — wider than 360px mobile viewports. Always use responsive padding like px-4 sm:px-12 for mobile-first components that also have max-width constraints.

**Why:** Issue #2138 edge case: LatexDocumentViewer used px-12 py-10 which is 48px horizontal padding. With max-w-[794px] inner content, the container overflows 360px viewports. The fix is px-4 sm:px-12 (16px on mobile, 48px on sm+).

**How to apply:** When adding padding to components that also have max-width or fixed-width constraints, always use sm: or md: responsive breakpoints for larger padding values.
